title: Probability semantics for a program
statement: For a nondeterministic register program $A$, an oracle, an input $x$, a guard $G$ on configurations, an initial configuration $a$, and a rational number $p$, define probability semantics to mean that $A$ terminates from $a$ under guard $G$ and that, for every natural number $N$ for which all length-$N$ choice strings halt from $a$, the probability of returning true is $p$ and the probability of returning false is $1-p$.
hypotheses_covered: Program $A$ is a nondeterministic register program
An input bit string $x$ is specified
A guard $G$ on configurations is specified
For each $N$, the probability equations are required when all length-$N$ choice strings halt
